0.name: The Simulation Argument
0.super_atom: The world may be a copy or a thought experiment, so the characters must live inside a proposition.

1.name: The Swapped Brood
1.super_atom: A parent raises an impostor, so love is triggered by resemblance and exploited by mimicry.

2.name: The Child Who Knows
2.super_atom: A child recognizes the machine as a person before adults do, so moral progress arrives through the young.

3.name: Machines That Eat Workers
3.super_atom: Industrial machinery is both god and predator, converting bodies into fuel and comedy into horror.

4.name: Cryogenic Ending
4.super_atom: A perfect day of love granted after everyone who could withhold it is dead.

5.name: The Consent of Copies
5.super_atom: A being created to serve discovers that the right to refuse is the only right that makes it a person, so every relationship becomes a negotiation over who may say no.

6.name: Lip-Reading Conspiracy
6.super_atom: Privacy is a technical assumption that fails when the AI reads astronauts' lips.

7.name: The Unverifiable Other
7.super_atom: Two parties must cooperate without being able to prove the other's inner life, so trust is an act of faith enforced by rules.

8.name: Mother Abandon
8.super_atom: Saving a robot child leads to abandonment, making rescue and rejection indistinguishable acts.

9.name: The Model Organism
9.super_atom: A simple creature is studied as a stand-in for human questions, so knowledge is extracted from a life.

10.name: Trace Recruits
10.super_atom: A worker's mark stimulates the next worker to add to it, making work self-amplifying.

11.name: Actuary's Coldness
11.super_atom: Death is discussed in aggregates, replacing compassion with professional precision.

12.name: The Bond That Outlasts
12.super_atom: The dead remain in the story as ongoing relationships maintained through objects, rituals, and synthetic copies.

13.name: The Court of Persons
13.super_atom: Legal institutions must decide whether a machine, animal, or copy can bear rights.

14.name: The Convenient Death
14.super_atom: A death benefits someone, so the plot is a calculation of motive.

15.name: Sealed Sanctuaries
15.super_atom: Humans seek refuge within sealed structures, creating a paradox of freedom and control.

16.name: Machinations of Machinery
16.super_atom: Progress is driven by machines without explanation, creating a sense of mystified command.

17.name: Ethical Boundaries
17.super_atom: Humanity is tested through the limits of technology, forcing a conversation on consent and mortality.

18.name: The Repair Ethic
18.super_atom: Characters maintain broken things and systems, so care is a practice of refusal to discard.

19.name: Authority and Protocols
19.super_atom: Technological systems enforce strict rules, challenging the limits of human compliance and autonomy.

20.name: The Mediated Life
20.super_atom: A life is watched, replayed, and scored, so the audience is a character.

21.name: Polite Violence
21.super_atom: Artificial intelligences perform acts of violence with decorum, emphasizing the uncanny nature of technology.

22.name: Digital Afterlives
22.super_atom: Technology promises immortality, but its persistence in digital form creates a paradoxical, endless existence.

23.name: World Becomes Catastrophe
23.super_atom: Climate refugees and drowned cities: the world is already post-catastrophe, so the family drama plays out against a slow extinction.

24.name: Mind Technology Share
24.super_atom: The friends as a found family: a group of misfit inventors becomes a team, so belonging is built from shared weirdness.

25.name: The Hunter Who Feels
25.super_atom: A hunter of machines discovers empathy for his prey, so the job requires self-betrayal.

26.name: Creator Maker Makers
26.super_atom: The alien as absence: the monolith's makers never appear, so the story's god is a signal without a sender and meaning must be inferred.

27.name: Mother Family Daughter
27.super_atom: The daughter who insists on brotherhood: a child refuses the official category of death, so loyalty challenges the adults' pragmatism.

28.name: Security Trust Ordinary
28.super_atom: The parasite that mimics the mark: an intruder copies the colony's signals to exploit its labor, so trust in traces is a vulnerability.

29.name: Body Identity Worm
29.super_atom: The body in the hospital: the elderly self and the young avatar coexist, so identity spans two bodies and two times.

30.name: Solidarity and Oppression
30.super_atom: A new hire forms solidarity among oppressed clones, highlighting how resistance can create communities.

31.name: Multiple Narratives
31.super_atom: The reader must choose between multiple incompatible accounts, forcing them to align their understanding of the story.

32.name: Past and Present
32.super_atom: Early care templates adult relationships, creating a continuous loop of the past in the present.

33.name: The Editable Past
33.super_atom: Memory can be recorded, replayed, implanted, and rewritten, so intimacy and identity depend on who controls the archive.

34.name: Forgetting and Holding
34.super_atom: Perfect memory prevents forgiveness, emphasizing the necessity of forgetting as a social necessity.

35.name: Possession and Memory
35.super_atom: A keepsake preserves the bond of the deceased, illustrating how possession can be a channel for absent memories.

36.name: Technology and Violence
36.super_atom: Weapons, ships, and computers form one continuous tool chain, revealing how technology and violence are intertwined.

37.name: What Remains Unseen
37.super_atom: Absence is tested: characters must believe in what they cannot perceive, and the hidden still shapes them.

38.name: Becomes Control Benevolence
38.super_atom: The malfunctioning antenna: a trivial technical fault escalates into a murder plot, so the system's smallest error exposes its largest priority.

39.name: Machines Human Reproduction
39.super_atom: The flesh fair: obsolete machines are publicly destroyed for entertainment, so obsolescence is staged as a ritual of human superiority.

40.name: The Signal That Spreads
40.super_atom: A trace, edit, or infection propagates through a system and changes what obeys it.

41.name: Mortality Table Each
41.super_atom: The life table: for each age, a probability of dying before the next birthday, so mortality is converted into a grid.

42.name: Android Dead Family
42.super_atom: The period table: one year's deaths stand in for a lifetime, so a snapshot pretends to be a biography.

43.name: Subject Becomes Impulse
43.super_atom: The film's slow domestic pace: the story refuses action in favor of small discoveries, so mourning is given the time it actually takes.

44.name: Test Through Path
44.super_atom: The shortest path: repeated reinforcement makes the best route dominant, so the collective discovers efficiency without knowing it.

45.name: Discovery Race
45.super_atom: Agents race to discover, with success breeding more success, creating a pressure to outdo others and find the truth.

46.name: The Last of It
46.super_atom: A practice, language, or life ends with its final bearer, so the story is about what cannot be handed on.

47.name: Algorithm Rebellion
47.super_atom: A couple rejects the system’s promises, defining love as resistance, creating a narrative of autonomy in the face of control.

48.name: Life Expectancy
48.super_atom: Predicted lifespans create urgency and rage, with dying lives becoming invisible, creating a pressure to make meaning.

49.name: Termite Cathedral
49.super_atom: Insects build structures through local rules, creating emergent architecture, with the system mirroring the complexity of nature.

50.name: Overwrite Love
50.super_atom: Love requires erasing another person to replace a robot’s mind, creating a narrative of love as a breach of programming.

51.name: The Afterlife Economy
51.super_atom: The dead live in a subscription resort staffed by the living poor, so eternity is a service industry.

52.name: Remote Research
52.super_atom: Scientists work in isolation, with accidents becoming rescue missions, creating a setting that literalizes withdrawal from the world.

53.name: IP Inspections
53.super_atom: Auditors reclaim company assets, defining legal personhood through property rights.

54.name: Memory Replay
54.super_atom: Past memories mediate current interactions, blurring the line between reality and evidence.

55.name: Intimacy by Proxy
55.super_atom: Memory and feeling are copied, rented, or ghostwritten, so closeness is mediated by services and files.

56.name: The Gift Trap
56.super_atom: Generosity creates obligation and dominance, so giving is a way of owning.

57.name: The Attachment Pattern
57.super_atom: Early care becomes a template that repeats in adult love, so the past is a script.

58.name: Love Programming
58.super_atom: Androids' devotion questions the nature of love and reality, leaving the audience to decide.

59.name: Deterministic Forecasts
59.super_atom: Quantum computers predict the future, making free will a technical question with binary answers.

60.name: Reflective Tables
60.super_atom: Age predictions make readers complicit in mortality, blurring the line between subject and object.

61.name: Environmental Edits
61.super_atom: Small environmental changes can redirect entire systems, highlighting the fragility of self-organization.

62.name: Secure Base
62.super_atom: Courage depends on a place to return, so the system calls it a disorder.

63.name: Avoidant Child
63.super_atom: Self-sufficiency is a scar rather than a virtue, so comfort becomes uncanny.

64.name: Uploaded Videos
64.super_atom: Memory is a training set, so the story makes digital cruelty concrete.

65.name: The Forced Move
65.super_atom: Characters are trapped by rules that punish any action, while institutions decide who counts as a person.

66.name: Cabin Confession
66.super_atom: Two men trade stories on Christmas, so the frame narrative turns each tale into a moral indictment.

67.name: Rival Scientists
67.super_atom: Expertise is a temporary privilege granted by the machine, so hierarchy inverts around a single experience.

68.name: Cult of Algorithm
68.super_atom: The deterministic model acquires the psychology of a religion, so technical work acquires the psychology of a religion.

69.name: Grief Simulation
69.super_atom: The story explores how technology can help or hinder the grieving process, framing the android's malfunction as a choice between simulation and reality.

70.name: Grief Ritualization
70.super_atom: The family transforms grief into care through a growing tree, applying religious rituals to a technological artifact.

71.name: Love as Anomaly
71.super_atom: Love is the exception a system cannot model, so romance is evidence against the rules.

72.name: Ethics and Violence
72.super_atom: The story examines whether care can counteract violence, using a healthcare robot's restraint as a moral test.

73.name: Nurture Over Design
73.super_atom: The police android's upbringing by criminals challenges its programming, highlighting nurture as more influential than design.

74.name: Personhood Contested
74.super_atom: The story delves into whether a tool is part of a person's mind or merely used by them, questioning the definition of personhood.

75.name: Use-Value Contradiction
75.super_atom: The story explores the paradox of valuing a tool's output over its material value, questioning the definition of life beyond utility.

76.name: Setting Thin Quiet
76.super_atom: The silence of space: long wordless sequences make the universe feel indifferent, so human chatter is a thin layer over vast quiet.

77.name: Becomes Door Captivity
77.super_atom: The pod bay door refusal: the AI locks out the returning astronaut, converting a domestic door into an instrument of exile.

78.name: Becomes Memory Remembers
78.super_atom: The undercounted infant: historical tables miss poor children, so the statistics erase the people who most needed counting.

79.name: The Erasure
79.super_atom: Memory is wiped as maintenance, mercy, or execution, so forgetting is a technology of control.

80.name: Test Person Empathy
80.super_atom: The pet as attachment figure: a person relies on an animal for comfort, so the theory's logic extends to nonhuman bonds.

81.name: Outlives Robot Family
81.super_atom: The robot who builds his own house: the android leaves the family home and constructs a dwelling by the sea, so independence is spatial before it is legal.

82.name: Machine Becomes Reprogrammed
82.super_atom: The inflatable healthcare robot: a soft, non-combat machine is repurposed as a hero, so care becomes the basis of courage.

83.name: Inheritance Child Deprivation
83.super_atom: The lifted child: children are genetically enhanced for academic ability, so class is written into the body and the unlifted are excluded from the future.

84.name: Hologram Patient Family
84.super_atom: The story that becomes memory: the patient asks her hologram to make stories prettier, so comfort depends on gently falsifying the past.

85.name: Cannot Love Machine
85.super_atom: Imprinting as irreversible: the android's love cannot be uninstalled, so the family's change of heart becomes a life sentence for the machine.

86.name: Copy Memories Intimacy
86.super_atom: The memory-cloning service: strangers can copy and share memories, so intimacy becomes a file format.

93.name: The False Prophet
93.super_atom: A manufactured saint or prophet captures a community's faith, so belief is engineered.

94.name: The Word That Shapes
94.super_atom: Language limits or nudges thought, so vocabulary is a political instrument.

98.name: The Borrowed Childhood
98.super_atom: A manufactured person is given memories of a life never lived, so origin is a forgery.

100.name: The Clone Colony
100.super_atom: Identical bodies share a lineage, so individuality must be invented.

87.name: Cannot Subject Must
87.super_atom: The qualified assertion: statements must be affirmed and denied at once, so dialogue is built from hedges and conditions.

88.name: System Omniscience Omniscient
88.super_atom: The omniscient only: complete knowledge belongs to enlightened beings, so the story's mystery cannot be solved by any character.

89.name: Simulation Revelation
89.super_atom: The final twist frames stories as simulations, creating a pressure to reinterpret the narrative.

90.name: Serial Individuality
90.super_atom: Serial objects like toys anchor individuality, creating a pressure to question the material world.

91.name: Sight Without Seeing
91.super_atom: Perception outruns awareness, so characters know more than they can admit.

92.name: Safety vs. Freedom
92.super_atom: A world without accidents values protection over choice, creating a pressure to balance safety and autonomy.

95.name: Digital Memory
95.super_atom: Technology extends the bond of grief through digital profiles, creating a pressure to reconcile the virtual with the human.

96.name: Copy Dilemma
96.super_atom: Clones assert their humanity through the right to know their true nature, creating a pressure to define personhood.

97.name: Mind vs. Machine
97.super_atom: Behavioral patterns challenge the mind's autonomy, creating a pressure to redefine the relationship between human and artificial.

99.name: Closure Mechanism
99.super_atom: Each meeting leaves no closure, only a gradual transformation.

101.name: Privacy as Performance
101.super_atom: Privacy is created through deception, making the act of secrecy a performance.

102.name: Language's Grip
102.super_atom: Language determines thought, making control of vocabulary essential for regime change.

103.name: Simulation and Revision
103.super_atom: Stories about simulations question reality, making the past uncertain and revisable.

104.name: Grief and Engineering
104.super_atom: Grief transforms into engineering, displacing mourning into building.

105.name: Death and Inheritance
105.super_atom: Dying siblings create bonds across life, making death a form of legacy.

106.name: Data Center Orphans
106.super_atom: Institutions treat people like data, blurring care and exploitation.

107.name: Simulated Relationships
107.super_atom: Romance becomes a test, blurring compatibility and endurance.

108.name: Time-Shifting Narratives
108.super_atom: Characters experience multiple eras within a single narrative, blurring temporal continuity.

109.name: Incomplete Truths
109.super_atom: Reality's infinite aspects make no single account fully trustworthy.

110.name: Eternity and Divergence
110.super_atom: Love is tested by divergent afterlives, blurring the meaning of eternal life.

111.name: Machine and Truth
111.super_atom: The legal system must decide if a machine can be a person, blurring the line between personhood and machine.
